subject: Causally restricted inference in time series

messages.author: 5b9291bf9c2e9978
messages.subject: Causally restricted inference in time series
parts:
Dear Stan Users,
I am trying to build a Stan model for human temporal learning of properties perceptual stimuli, assuming that the observer is performing optimal inference.

In short, given a time series data_{1:N}, I am interested in inferring the 'conditional' posterior of a latent variable Sn after each data point P(S_n|data_{1:n}),  P(S_{n+1}|data_{1:n+1}),  P(S_{n+2}|data_{1:n+2}) etc. (Actual model attached. Could do with some vectorisation for speed-up).
I.e. an agent has to make a decision based on the posterior of Sn before receiving future data (causality).
This is opposed to getting the final posterior P(S_{1:N}|data_{1:N}) for which the posterior over S_n depends on the data received after time point n.

I could run the fitting of the model with data 1, with data 1:2, with data 1:3 ... but running Stan N(~1500) times seems extremely inefficient and slow (and speed matters in my application).

If I had an analytical expression of the posterior I could of course use an iterative approach (P(S_{n+1}|data_{1:n+1})=P(data_{n+1}|S_{n+1},data_n|)P(S_{n+1}|data_n)/Z (given a model of P(S_{n+1}|S_n) ), or similarly just updating the posterior. 

Is there something equivalent that can be done in STAN,  or is there some way of writing out a model so that samples of S_n can be recorded before knowledge of data n+1 is used? (I have a feeling that I am just missing the right term to search for, sorry!)

Thanks for any comments!

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Causally restricted inference in time series
parts:
There's no way to directly implement what you're asking for
in Stan's object language given the way you've coded the model.
We treat all the parameters jointly and update them all
at the same time.

You could jam everything into a single model with parameters for
each data slice 1:N, but it wouldn't be pretty and it'd probably be slower
than running 1500 independent models and would definitely be a memory
hog. Do you really need all 1500 predictions?

Or you could hope for conjugacy as you suggest, but then you
probably wouldn't need MCMC at all!

What you're looking for is related to the cut function in BUGS, but
I don't think cut would let you do what you need, either.

- Bob

Thanks!
Ulrik
